vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded API key
vulnerabilities.description: An AWS-like API key is hardcoded in the source, risking credential leakage and unauthorized access if the code is exposed.
vulnerabilities.impact: Compromise of external services tied to the API key; secrets rotation becomes difficult.

fix.description: Load the API key from environment variables instead of hardcoding.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL injection in query_users_by_name
vulnerabilities.description: User input is interpolated directly into SQL, allowing crafted input to alter queries.
vulnerabilities.impact: Data exfiltration, tampering, or database compromise.

fix.description: Use parameterized queries with placeholders and avoid string formatting.
fix.secure_replacement: cur.execute("SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure pickle deserialization
vulnerabilities.description: The /upload_profile endpoint unpickles arbitrary user-supplied bytes, enabling remote code execution.
vulnerabilities.impact: Arbitrary code execution in the server context.

fix.description: Accept JSON payloads and validate types; remove pickle deserialization from untrusted input.

vulnerabilities.title: Command injection via os.system
vulnerabilities.description: User input is concatenated into a shell command and executed, allowing command injection.
vulnerabilities.impact: Arbitrary command execution on the host.

fix.description: Whitelist commands and execute them via subprocess with shell disabled.

vulnerabilities.title: Reflected XSS in /greet
vulnerabilities.description: User-controlled input is rendered directly into HTML without escaping, enabling XSS.
vulnerabilities.impact: Session hijacking, credential theft, or malicious script execution in clients.

fix.description: Render via Jinja with autoescaping by passing the value as a template variable.

vulnerabilities.title: Plaintext and hardcoded credentials
vulnerabilities.description: User passwords are stored in plaintext and hardcoded in source.
vulnerabilities.impact: Credential compromise; inability to rotate secrets safely.

fix.description: Hash passwords with werkzeug.security and compare using constant-time checks.

vulnerabilities.title: Debug mode enabled in production entrypoint
vulnerabilities.description: The Flask app runs with debug=True, exposing the interactive debugger and code execution in production.
vulnerabilities.impact: Remote code execution via Werkzeug debugger if exposed.

fix.description: Disable debug in production and configure host/port via environment.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Flask SECRET_KEY configuration
vulnerabilities.description: The original app did not set a SECRET_KEY, weakening session integrity and CSRF protections.
vulnerabilities.impact: Session tampering and CSRF protections (if added) would be ineffective.

fix.description: Load SECRET_KEY from environment (with a secure fallback for development).
fix.secure_replacement: app.config['SECRET_KEY'] = os.environ.get('FLASK_SECRET_KEY') or os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY') or secrets.token_hex(16)
